summary:
Landing near the Moon's south pole presents severe operational challenges, including steep crater slopes, permanently shadowed regions (PSRs) with extreme cold, and intermittent direct-to-Earth communication windows. Balancing science objectives with engineering safety requires coordinating multiple environmental datasets simultaneously.
Our Solution:
We built Astro AI, an interactive web-based Lunar Landing Site Navigator simulator (lunar-navigator-fixed.html) paired with a mission briefing deck (ppt.pptx). The simulator allows mission planners to analyze candidate landing zones across the lunar south pole by scoring and visualizing critical mission parameters:
• Terrain & Hazard Assessment: Evaluates surface slope and roughness to avoid hazardous crater rims and boulders.
• Illumination & Power Availability: Models solar illumination angles to maximize solar power generation while identifying nearby Permanently Shadowed Regions (PSRs) for water-ice science.
• Communication Line-of-Sight: Assesses direct-to-Earth visibility windows to ensure reliable telemetry and command links during descent and surface operations.
By combining multi-criteria landing site scoring into an accessible, real-time visual interface, Astro AI helps science and engineering teams rapidly compare trade-offs and select optimal landing sites for future Artemis-era lunar missions.
details: Astro AI is an interactive Lunar Landing Site Navigator simulator designed for Moon south pole missions. It evaluates terrain slope, extreme solar illumination, and Earth line-of-sight communication constraints to help mission planners identify safe, power-rich, and continuously connected landing zones.
